html:
The Wounaan are an Indigenous people of the Pacific rainforest of the Chocó region of Colombia and the Darién of Panama. Together with the closely related Emberá, they were long called Chocó.

They live along rivers in houses on stilts, travel by dugout canoe, and farm plantains and maize, fish and hunt. Wounaan women weave very fine baskets of palm fibre, and men carve the dark cocobolo wood; these crafts are now an important source of income. In 1983 Panama created the Emberá-Wounaan comarca, a self-governing territory, in the Darién. Their neighbours to the west include the Ngäbe and Buglé and the Guna.
